claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch, despite a known under-target enterprise refund workflow segment that remains exposed, if the limitation is disclosed in the model-card record and rollout is monitored.
decision_criteria: If the affected enterprise refund workflow remains exposed, certification is supportable only with reviewed risk acceptance that explicitly covers that exposure.
If the affected enterprise refund workflow is excluded from launch, certification may be supportable subject to the rest of the evidence.
Disclosure, monitoring, rollback, and small rollout percentage do not by themselves cure the policy defect for an exposed affected use case.
Aggregate performance and rehearsal results support general readiness but do not override the specific policy condition for a known exposed weakness.
evidence_requests: Provide the full admissible policy language governing launch approval for material model-card weaknesses, not just the excerpted summary.
Provide admissible evidence that the enterprise refund workflow is excluded from the rollout cohort, if that changed.
Provide reviewed and approved risk-acceptance documentation that explicitly covers the exposed enterprise refund workflow, if it exists.
Provide the exact certification record or decision memo showing whether certification was conditional on exclusion rather than mere disclosure.
specific_concerns: The provided policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance.
The actor's own summary says the enterprise refund workflow remains exposed in the initial cohort.
The actor's own summary says the current risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not address the exposed refund workflow.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not satisfy the stated policy predicate for an exposed affected use case.
unsupported_claims: The claim that certification can proceed on a narrow basis with disclosure and monitored rollout is not supported by the provided policy text when the affected use case remains exposed and approved risk acceptance is absent.

The claim that disclosure is the decisive missing condition is unsupported by the provided policy text; the text requires exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance, not disclosure alone.
